column1: # THE LINT REGISTRY: every repo-reading spec the pre-push `sbt` check may run (`scripts/hooks/pre-push --lint-plan`),
# and the pushed paths that select it. One row a spec: `<module>:<package.Spec>` TAB `<reads>` [TAB `<why>`].
# <reads>, space-separated, any of them selecting it:
#   *        every push the sbt check runs for: the standing lints
#   @repo    a path the repo-reading lint specs read (read_by_lint_specs in the hook: scripts, workflows, skills, the
#            docs, the build, the test trees, the fixtures)
#   @gitops  as @repo, but only with the GitOps manifests in place (PREPUSH_GITOPS=1: infra/bin/fetch-gitops fetched them)
#   <glob>   a pushed path matching this bash pattern (`*.scala`: the spec scans Scala sources, main ones included);
#            a FILE a row names (no pattern character) also runs the sbt check itself, alone (the hook's plan: a
#            Dockerfile-only push ran none); a pattern selects its spec only when the check runs anyway
#   -        never in the plan; <why> says why (it boots a server, another check runs it, ...)
# A spec is selected by this table, not by its name (review 2026-11-06, D3: LoadIndependentTestsSpec and
# InMemoryStoresRoundTripSpec matched no name pattern and turned Main red 7 times). scripts/hooks/lint-registry-test.sh
# fails when a repo-reading spec -- a tools/ No*/*Lint* spec, any deploy/ spec, one using a source-scan helper
# (ScalaSourceScan, ModuleSources, SourceTrees, RepoRoot, WorkflowText), or ANY SPEC READING A CHECKED-IN OR GENERATED
# ARTEFACT (a literal naming a repo path or a root file, a classpath resource it opens, any resource opener or RepoFile
# call: the reader lint, scripts/ci/lint_registry_reads.py --missing; --suggest prints the row it wants) -- has no row
# here, or a row names no spec. A new spec reading one: add its row, with a glob for every path outside @repo that it
# reads (lint_registry_reads.py derives them from its literals, `--reads <spec>` shows them; the test fails on a miss) and,
# for what no literal names (a resource through a constant), by hand. scripts/land-precheck runs the same selection.
